summary: Equipment (Sprzet) feature tested end-to-end. 27/27 backend pytest cases pass covering CRUD, assignment matrix with quantity constraint, foreman my-equipment, full transfer flow (request/accept/reject with quantity movement), defects with role-scoped visibility, and history with admin/foreman scoping. Admin frontend Sprzet tab verified live: tab visible, add-equipment modal works, equipment card renders, assignment matrix renders for active foremen, history panel and defects panel render correctly.

issues: Pre-existing Google Maps ApiProjectMapError console error on dashboard load - unrelated to Sprzet feature

critical_code_review_comments: routes/equipment.py POST /equipment/assign uses query param `equipment_id` instead of putting it in the body alongside foreman_id/quantity - mixing query and body for related fields is unusual; consider unifying into the body for cleaner API.

POST /equipment/transfers/{id}/accept and /reject have no role check - any authenticated user (including admin) could call them but is gated by the `to_foreman_id == current_user.sub` check which means admin would always 403. Acceptable but consider explicit foreman role check for clarity.

The accept_transfer endpoint does NOT re-check that the receiver's new total + others <= equipment.total_quantity. While total system quantity is preserved (decrement source by qty, increment dest by qty) so it's mathematically safe, an extra defensive check would be robust if equipment.total_quantity were lowered between request and accept (currently blocked by update validator).

EquipmentForeman.js fetches /foremen list which returns ALL foremen including the current one - the transfer-to-select includes current user as a transfer target, but backend validates self-transfer; UI could filter current user out of dropdown for better UX.

EquipmentAdmin.js handleAssignChange uses defaultValue + onBlur - if user types same value as before, the strict-not-equals check prevents API call, which is good; but if user types a value, blurs, then re-edits, the input still shows the previously typed value rather than the fetched server value because defaultValue only applies on first render. After fetchAll() updates `assignments`, the input does NOT reset because of defaultValue. Consider using value+onChange or a key prop tied to assignment.
Equipment routes file is 482 lines - acceptable but approaching threshold; consider splitting transfer/defect logic into separate modules if it grows.
